question: Explain the classic NLP Preprocessing Pipeline: Tokenization, Stemming (Porter Stemmer) vs Lemmatization (WordNet), Stopwords, and POS Tagging.
idealAnswer: Stemming strips word suffixes via heuristic rule algorithms (e.g. 'running' -> 'run', 'better' -> 'better'; fast, non-words possible). Lemmatization reduces words to their valid vocabulary base lemma using morphological analysis and POS tags ('better' -> 'good').

explanation: Evaluates NLP Text Preprocessing and Stemming vs Lemmatization & Tokenization comprehension.

question: Explain Bag-of-Words (BoW) and N-Grams vs TF-IDF (Term Frequency - Inverse Document Frequency) for document representation.
idealAnswer: Bag-of-Words counts raw word occurrences, ignoring syntax and order. N-grams capture local word sequences (bi-grams, tri-grams). TF-IDF weights words by term frequency scaled by inverse document frequency (log(N/df)), downweighting common words and highlighting distinctive domain terms.
ideal_answer: Bag-of-Words counts raw word occurrences, ignoring syntax and order. N-grams capture local word sequences (bi-grams, tri-grams). TF-IDF weights words by term frequency scaled by inverse document frequency (log(N/df)), downweighting common words and highlighting distinctive domain terms.
explanation: Evaluates NLP Vectorization and TF-IDF vs Bag-of-Words comprehension.

question: Explain Word Embeddings: Word2Vec (Skip-Gram vs CBOW), GloVe (Global Vectors), and FastText (Subword n-grams for OOV words).
idealAnswer: Word2Vec Skip-Gram predicts context words from target word; CBOW predicts target word from context. GloVe factorizes global word co-occurrence matrices. FastText represents words as character n-grams, enabling embeddings for out-of-vocabulary (OOV) words and misspellings.
ideal_answer: Word2Vec Skip-Gram predicts context words from target word; CBOW predicts target word from context. GloVe factorizes global word co-occurrence matrices. FastText represents words as character n-grams, enabling embeddings for out-of-vocabulary (OOV) words and misspellings.
explanation: Evaluates NLP Embeddings and Word2Vec vs GloVe vs FastText comprehension.

question: What is Subword Tokenization (Byte-Pair Encoding - BPE, WordPiece, Unigram, SentencePiece), and why is it preferred over character-level or word-level tokenization?
idealAnswer: Word-level tokenization causes huge vocabularies and out-of-vocabulary failures. Character-level tokenization causes very long sequences. Subword algorithms (BPE in GPT, WordPiece in BERT) iteratively merge frequent character pairs, maintaining compact ~50K vocabularies while breaking rare words into recognizable subwords.
ideal_answer: Word-level tokenization causes huge vocabularies and out-of-vocabulary failures. Character-level tokenization causes very long sequences. explanation: Evaluates NLP Tokenization and Subword Tokenization (BPE & WordPiece) comprehension.

question: Compare BERT (Bidirectional Encoder Representations from Transformers) and GPT (Generative Pre-trained Transformer) in training objectives (MLM vs Causal LM).
idealAnswer: BERT is an Encoder model trained bi-directionally on Masked Language Modeling (MLM - predicting random 15% masked tokens) and Next Sentence Prediction (optimal for classification/NER). GPT is an autoregressive Decoder model trained on causal next-token prediction (optimal for generation).

GPT is an autoregressive Decoder model trained on causal next-token prediction (optimal for generation).
explanation: Evaluates NLP Transformer Models and BERT vs GPT Architectures comprehension.

question: Explain Named Entity Recognition (NER): BIO/IOB Tagging scheme, CRF (Conditional Random Fields), and BERT-based token classification.
idealAnswer: NER extracts entity mentions (Person, Org, Location). BIO tagging annotates tokens: B (Begin entity), I (Inside entity), O (Outside). Linear-chain CRFs or BERT token classification heads model transition probabilities between sequential tags to ensure valid sequence predictions.

question: How do you evaluate Machine Translation and Text Summarization using BLEU, ROUGE (ROUGE-1, ROUGE-2, ROUGE-L), and METEOR scores?
idealAnswer: BLEU evaluates precision of n-gram overlaps between generated text and reference translations (penalizing short translations). ROUGE evaluates recall (ROUGE-1 word recall, ROUGE-2 bigram recall, ROUGE-L longest common subsequence) primarily used in text summarization.
ideal_answer: BLEU evaluates precision of n-gram overlaps between generated text and reference translations (penalizing short translations). ROUGE evaluates recall (ROUGE-1 word recall, ROUGE-2 bigram recall, ROUGE-L longest common subsequence) primarily used in text summarization.
explanation: Evaluates NLP NLP Evaluation and BLEU vs ROUGE Scores comprehension.

question: Explain Sentiment Analysis and Aspect-Based Sentiment Analysis (ABSA) for extracting opinions on specific entity attributes.
idealAnswer: Standard sentiment analysis classifies overall document/sentence polarity (positive, negative, neutral). Aspect-Based Sentiment Analysis (ABSA) extracts specific aspect terms (e.g. 'battery life', 'screen display') and determines the sentiment polarity targeted at each individual aspect.

Aspect-Based Sentiment Analysis (ABSA) extracts specific aspect terms (e.g. 'battery life', 'screen display') and determines the sentiment polarity targeted at each individual aspect.
explanation: Evaluates NLP Sentiment & Classification and Aspect-Based Sentiment Analysis comprehension.

question: Explain Topic Modeling: Latent Dirichlet Allocation (LDA) and BERTopic (Transformer embeddings + UMAP + HDBSCAN + c-TF-IDF).
idealAnswer: LDA is a probabilistic model assuming documents are mixtures of topics and topics are distributions over words. BERTopic uses Transformer embeddings to capture semantic context, clusters embeddings with UMAP dimensionality reduction and HDBSCAN, and extracts topic keywords using class-based TF-IDF (c-TF-IDF).
ideal_answer: LDA is a probabilistic model assuming documents are mixtures of topics and topics are distributions over words. BERTopic uses Transformer embeddings to capture semantic context, clusters embeddings with UMAP dimensionality reduction and HDBSCAN, and extracts topic keywords using class-based TF-IDF (c-TF-IDF).
explanation: Evaluates NLP Topic Modeling and LDA vs BERTopic comprehension.

question: What is Cross-Encoder vs Bi-Encoder (Sentence-BERT / SBERT) for semantic text similarity and semantic search?
idealAnswer: Bi-Encoders (SBERT) encode queries and documents independently into fixed dense vectors, enabling fast cosine similarity searches against millions of pre-computed document embeddings in vector stores. Cross-Encoders pass query and document together through full cross-attention for higher accuracy at significant compute cost.
ideal_answer: Bi-Encoders (SBERT) encode queries and documents independently into fixed dense vectors, enabling fast cosine similarity searches against millions of pre-computed document embeddings in vector stores. Cross-Encoders pass query and document together through full cross-attention for higher accuracy at significant compute cost.
explanation: Evaluates NLP Semantic Search and Bi-Encoder vs Cross-Encoder (SBERT) comprehension.

question: Explain the Seq2Seq (Sequence-to-Sequence) Architecture with Bahdanau (Additive) Attention vs Luong (Multiplicative) Attention.
idealAnswer: Seq2Seq encodes variable-length input sequences into context vectors for decoder generation. Bahdanau (additive) attention computes alignment scores using a feedforward layer and concatenates context with previous hidden state. Luong (multiplicative) attention uses dot products, simplifying calculation.

explanation: Evaluates NLP Seq2Seq and Bahdanau vs Luong Attention comprehension.

question: How does Text Generation Decoding work: Greedy Search, Beam Search, Temperature, Top-K, and Top-P sampling?
idealAnswer: Greedy search picks the highest probability token at each step (can get stuck in repetitive loops). Beam Search tracks B top candidate beams simultaneously (great for translation). Nucleus/Top-P and Top-K sampling introduce controlled randomness, producing natural conversational outputs.

question: What is Question Answering: Extractive QA (Span prediction with start/end logits) vs Abstractive QA (Generative Seq2Seq)?
idealAnswer: Extractive QA (e.g. BERT on SQuAD) predicts the exact start and end token indices of the answer span within a provided reference context passage. Abstractive QA generates a novel paraphrased natural language response from scratch using generative language models.
ideal_answer: Extractive QA (e.g. BERT on SQuAD) predicts the exact start and end token indices of the answer span within a provided reference context passage. Abstractive QA generates a novel paraphrased natural language response from scratch using generative language models.

question: Explain Coreference Resolution and Anaphora Resolution in NLP discourse processing.
idealAnswer: Coreference resolution identifies all expressions in text that refer to the same real-world entity (e.g. linking 'Elon Musk', 'the CEO', and 'he' in a multi-paragraph article). Mention clustering algorithms group detected pronoun and noun phrase mentions into entity clusters.

question: What is Perplexity in Language Modeling, and how does it measure cross-entropy loss on evaluation test corpora?
idealAnswer: Perplexity is the standard intrinsic evaluation metric for language models: defined as the exponential of the cross-entropy loss (PPL = exp(loss)). It represents the effective branching factor—a lower perplexity means the model is less surprised by test tokens and predicts text more accurately.
